correctness.rationale: Apply Garity-Repovs 2013 Theorem 4.7: wedge complement pi1 unchanged when second factor has simply-connected complement. Theorem 5.4: off wedge point local genera remain those of the factors, while at wedge point genera add g_x(C)+1 <=B+1. GRW 2014 rigid genus-one generalized Bing-Whitehead family gives every point of X_s genus1 and pairwise inequivalent X_s, simply-connected complements. Genus-one locus of Y_s comprises finite genus1 points from C away from wedge, the perfect X_s minus wedge, plus wedge precisely if g_x(C)=0. Thus inherited C points are isolated in L1 while points of X_s except wedge are nonisolated, and closure of derived set of L1 equals X_s. Ambient equivalence preserves local genus and this distinguished closed subset, inducing forbidden equivalence between X_s and X_t; if C is rigid, each self-homeomorphism fixing both rigid factors fixes Y_s. Proof uses only the stated finite F assumption; no construction of a nontrivial-complement base is asserted.

value.rationale: The finite-genus-one-locus condition is a natural geometric restriction motivated by Garity-Repovs bounded-genus question and finite-genus-one questions. The factor-recovery lemma via the derived genus-one locus yields an explicit uncountable family of inequivalent embeddings with controlled local genus and fixed complement fundamental group for every base C satisfying the hypothesis. This conditional extension is structurally useful even though it does not resolve existence for arbitrary prescribed nontrivial groups.

limitations: Conditional on bounded local genus and finite genus-one locus in base C, not a general solution of 2013 Question 8.1.
No claims of nontrivial complement-group base existence for every group or of rigidity unless C itself is rigid.
